note: MAIN HAS TEN RED HEAVY-TIER TESTS AND THEY ARE NOT ANY ONE CAMPAIGNs. Measured 2026-08-28 by bisecting each failure in scratch worktrees at two SHAs -- 7576eca00, before The Sources branched at all, and cae086f86 -- and every one of these ten reproduces identically at both. Eight hearsay probes (probe_seam_direction x2, probe_crossing_scale, probe_tiebreak_rules, probe_argmin_defect_crossing_arms, parley_readout, undertow_readout, touchstone_readout; 5780 vs 4975, touchstone 23 vs 10), radiation_readout each_elf_concentrates (settlement counts 41 to 4, 11 to 6, 7 to 2), and disposition_calibration the_sub_floor_raider_reading_is_pinned_as_a_witness (12 of 60 to 10 of 60). WHY NOBODY HAS NOTICED: decision 0148 took heavy off the merge phase list, gate-commit does not include it, and the stage gate does not either -- so nothing runs it unless a human types make heavy-remote, and the committed seam-guard roster cannot tell you when that last happened. A campaign that moves world numbers can therefore ship green through every gate it is asked to pass and still leave these red. THE TRAP THIS SETS FOR THE NEXT CAMPAIGN, and it nearly caught mine: if you run heavy after moving world values, you will see these ten alongside your own and the natural move is to regenerate them all. Do not. Bisect first -- run each failure standalone at your branch point. Nine of the ten I was told were mine were not, and re-pinning them would have written this campaigns name into dated prose on breakage that predates it. Full attribution table in The Sources retrospective.
